Derive approximate boundaries by dissolving a spatial frame

Source: R/admin_map.R
dissolve_frame_boundaries.Rd

When no boundary file is available, the sampling units themselves can stand in for administrative units. Neither result is an administrative border, and the difference matters:

dissolve_frame_boundaries(frame, level = "adm3", method = c("union", "hull"))

Arguments

frame

Path to a polygon frame, or an sf object of sampling units. A point layer works for method = "hull".

level

Column of frame holding the administrative unit.

method

"union" for the sampled footprint, "hull" for one convex hull per unit.

Value

An sf object with a name column and a derived attribute recording the method.

Details

  • method = "union" dissolves the sampling units into their sampled footprint. It is truthful about where the frame actually placed units, and on a gridded-population frame it is a scatter of small patches – fine for showing extent, useless as a choropleth.

  • method = "hull" takes the convex hull of each unit, giving one contiguous readable shape per unit. It overstates the area covered and neighbouring hulls can overlap, but it is legible, and it is what plot_psu_map() already draws behind the sampling units.

Prefer a real boundary file through read_admin_boundaries() whenever one exists; these are fallbacks, and the function says so.

See also

Other PSU maps: admin_map_data(), plot_admin_map(), plot_admin_progress_bars(), plot_psu_map(), psu_map_data(), psu_map_summary(), read_admin_boundaries(), read_psu_frame()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
bd <- dissolve_frame_boundaries("PSU_segments.geojson", level = "adm3")
bd <- dissolve_frame_boundaries("PSU_segments.geojson", method = "hull")
} # }
